1.title: Device Groups, Automation Levels and Security Policies with ASR Rules
1.text: Welcome to Module three: Device Groups, Automation Levels and Security Policies with A S R Rules. It covers the exam area one. Manage a security operations environment. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. Configure and manage device groups, permissions and automation levels in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint. Configure security policies for Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, including attack surface reduction (A S R) rules. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: one. Manage a security operations environment (forty to forty-five percent). Exam format: one hundred minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official Microsoft S C-two hundred study guide and Microsoft Learn.

1.title: Device groups
1.text: Device groups. Path: Settings, then Endpoints, then Permissions, then Device groups. A tenant can have up to two thousand device groups. A device group sets who can see the devices and how much remediation is automatic.

1.title: Device groups, continued
1.text: Device groups. The figure shows this: A device joins the highest-ranked group it matches.

1.title: Device groups, continued
1.text: Device groups. General. Name, remediation (automation) level, description. Devices. Match rules on device name, domain, tags, O S platform; a device must match all the conditions. Preview devices. Shows up to ten matching devices. User access. The Microsoft Entra user groups that can see the devices.

1.title: Device groups, continued
1.text: Device groups. Several values for one property. Combined with or; up to ten rows per property type. Rank. Rank one is highest; a device that matches several groups joins only the highest-ranked one. Ungrouped devices (default). Cannot be ranked or deleted; you can change its automation level and access. No Entra group assigned. The device group is visible to all users. Exam tip: A device lands in exactly one group: the highest-ranked match. Rank one wins. Devices that match nothing go to Ungrouped devices.

1.title: Automation levels
1.text: Automation levels. The automation level decides what automated investigation may remediate without a person. Full - remediate threats automatically. No approval; recommended. Semi - require approval for core folders remediation. Approval needed only for core (system) folders. Semi - require approval for non-temp folders remediation. Approval needed for everything except temporary folders. Semi - require approval for all folders. Approval needed for all folders. No automated response. No automated investigation or remediation; also disables automatic attack disruption for the group.

1.title: Automation levels, continued
1.text: Automation levels. The device group wizard shows slightly different names for the same levels (for example Semi - Approval required for system folders). The meaning is the same. Default (new tenants). Full for tenants created on or after August sixteen, twenty twenty with no device groups. Default (older tenants). Semi - require approval for all folders. Pending actions. Time out after seven days and are treated as rejected. Where to approve. Action center, then Pending (approve or reject); History shows past actions and lets you undo some. Exam tip: Pending approvals expire after seven days. No automated response also stops automatic attack disruption for that group (Module four).

1.title: Roles and permissions
1.text: Roles and permissions. Turn on R back. A Security Administrator starts it. Global Administrator. Unrestricted access regardless of device groups. Security Reader. Loses access after R back is on until assigned a role. Approve device remediation. Active remediation actions (Defender for Endpoint role) or Security operations Security data Response (manage) (unified R back). Create notification rules. Manage security settings. Exam tip: To let an analyst approve remediation and nothing else, give the response (manage) permission scoped to the right device groups.

1.title: Security policies and ASR rules
1.text: Security policies and A S R rules. Attack surface reduction (A S R) rules block risky behaviors such as Office apps starting child processes. They need Defender Antivirus as primary and active, with real-time protection and cloud-delivered protection on. Not configured. five. Disabled (Off). zero. Block. one. Audit. two. Warn. six (the user can click Unblock for twenty-four hours). Standard protection rules, safe to block without an audit phase: block abuse of exploited vulnerable signed drivers, block credential stealing from the L sass process, block persistence through W M I event subscription. Warn is not supported for the L sass rule or for the Office code-injection rule.

1.title: Security policies and ASR rules, continued
1.text: Security policies and A S R rules. Block credential stealing from the Windows local security authority subsystem. Dumping credentials from the L sass process. Block all Office applications from creating child processes. A document or macro launching other programs. Block executable content from email client and webmail. Executables and scripts opened straight from mail. Block execution of potentially obfuscated scripts. Obfuscated Java Script, V B Script or Power Shell. Block Win thirty-two A P I calls from Office macros. Macros that call Win thirty-two A P Is to run code. Block persistence through W M I event subscription. Fileless persistence through W M I. Every rule has a G U I D. Power Shell and custom policies identify a rule by its G U I D in -Attack Surface Reduction Rules Ids; you do not need to memorize the gooey Ds.

1.title: Deploying ASR rules
1.text: Deploying A S R rules. In tune endpoint security, Attack surface reduction policy. Recommended; assigned to device groups. Defender portal endpoint security policies. Same policy type from the Defender portal. In tune custom profile (O M A-U R I), other M D M. Through the Policy C S P. Configuration Manager, Group Policy. Group Policy path: Microsoft Defender Antivirus, then Microsoft Defender Exploit Guard, then Attack Surface Reduction. Power Shell. Set-Mp Preference overwrites the rule list; Add-Mp Preference adds; Remove-Mp Preference removes. Power Shell uses -Attack Surface Reduction Rules Ids and -Attack Surface Reduction Rules Actions (Enabled, Audit Mode, Warn, Disabled, Not Configured). Group Policy and M D M overwrite local Power Shell settings.

1.title: Deploying ASR rules, continued
1.text: Deploying A S R rules. Global A S R rule exclusions. All methods (-Attack Surface Reduction Only Exclusions in Power Shell). Per-rule exclusions. Group Policy, In tune endpoint security, Defender portal only.

1.title: Monitoring ASR rules
1.text: Monitoring A S R rules. Reports, then Endpoints, then Attack surface reduction rules (or security.microsoft.com or asr). Tabs Detections, Configuration, Add exclusions; needs Plan two or Defender for Business. Advanced hunting. Table Device Events, filter Action Type startswith "Asr"; audit events end with Audited. Event Viewer. Audit events such as I D one thousand one hundred twenty-two. Exam tip: Audit first, then Block. The A S R report and Device Events with Action Type starting with Asr show what a rule would have blocked.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A Windows eleven laptop has the tag Finance and matches two device groups: a group ranked one and a group ranked three. Which group does the device join? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: The group ranked one, because the highest rank wins. A device joins only the highest-ranked group it matches, and rank one is highest.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A new tenant was created in twenty twenty-five and has no device groups. Which automation level applies by default? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Full - remediate threats automatically. Tenants created on or after August sixteen, twenty twenty with no device groups default to full automation.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A remediation action waits in the Action center and nobody approves it. What happens after seven days? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: The action times out and is treated as rejected. Pending actions time out after seven days and are treated as rejected.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. An administrator wants to add an A S R rule in audit mode with Power Shell without removing the rules already configured. Which cmdlet should be used? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Add-Mp Preference, which appends to the existing rule list. Add-Mp Preference adds rules; Set-Mp Preference overwrites the list.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. An analyst must see which A S R rules would have blocked activity in audit mode, in a portal report. Where should the analyst look? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Reports, then Endpoints, then Attack surface reduction rules. The A S R rules report has Detections, Configuration and Add exclusions tabs.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A team needs an exclusion that applies to one A S R rule only, not to all rules. Which deployment methods support a per-rule exclusion? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Group Policy, In tune endpoint security or the Defender portal. Per-rule exclusions are supported by Group Policy, In tune endpoint security and the Defender portal.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is the maximum number of device groups per tenant? Answer: two thousand. Question two. Which rank is the highest? Answer: Rank one. Question three. After how long do pending actions time out? Answer: seven days (treated as rejected).

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which A S R mode lets users unblock for twenty-four hours? Answer: Warn. Question five. Which cmdlet overwrites the A S R rule list? Answer: Set-Mp Preference. Question six. Which hunting table holds A S R events? Answer: Device Events (Action Type starts with Asr).

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Device groups: Settings, then Endpoints, then Permissions, then Device groups; two thousand max; rank one wins. Automation levels: Full, three Semi levels, No automated response; pending actions expire in seven days. Approve: Active remediation actions or Response (manage). A S R modes: zero off, one block, two audit, five not configured, six warn. Deploy: In tune endpoint security (recommended), Group Policy, Power Shell Add or Set. Monitor: A S R report, Device Events Action Type Asr. If this course is helping you, please subscribe to the channel and hit the bell icon, so you get a notification when the next video is out. In the next module, we continue the course.
